questions.question: In ∆ DEW, AB∥EW. If AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm and DW = 24 cm, then find the length of DB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ∆DEW, AB∥EW.

AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm, DW = 24 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Using the Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT):

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, then it divides those sides in the same ratio.

**Calculation:**

Using BPT, we have:

(AD)/(DE) = (DB)/(DW)

Substitute the given values:

(4)/(12) = (DB)/(24)

Simplify the ratio on the left side:

(1)/(3) = (DB)/(24)

Cross-multiply to solve for DB:

⇒ DB × 3 = 24

⇒ DB = 24 / 3

⇒ DB = 8 cm

**The length of DB is 8 cm.**

questions.question: Two triangles XYZ and UVW are congruent. If the area of ΔXYZ is 58 cm², then the area of ΔUVW will be:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Two triangles XYZ and UVW are congruent

The area of ΔXYZ = 58 cm2

**Concept used**

Two triangles are said to be congruent if their sides have the same length and their angles have the same measure.

Thus, two triangles can be superimposed side to side and angle to angle.

**Calculation**

Congruent triangles are triangles having corresponding sides and angles to be equal.

Congruence is denoted by the symbol “≅”. From the above concept, we can write XYZ ≅ UVW.

**They have the same area and the same perimeter.**

**The answer is 58.**

questions.question: If ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar. AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm and RP = 24 cm, then the perimeter of ΔABC is _________ cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

Ratio of corresponding sides = AB / PQ = 8 / 12 = 2 / 3

Perimeter of ΔABC = 54 × (2 / 3) = 36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB = 8 cm

PQ = 12 cm

QR = 18 cm

RP = 24 cm

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

**Formula Used:**

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides:

Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ = BC / QR = CA / RP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c915b7e6c39814636414cedc3eaca66decb41a196ad73642c855739f7673ffdb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 8 / 12

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 2 / 3

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 54 × (2 / 3)

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 18 × 2 = 36 cm

**Option Analysis:**

**Option (1) 36:** This is the correct perimeter of ΔABC as calculated above.

**Option (2) 54:** This is the perimeter of ΔPQR, not ΔABC.

**Option (3) 27:** This value is incorrect because the ratio of perimeters must be 2:3, which gives 36 cm, not 27 cm.

**Option (4) 42:** This value is incorrect because it does not satisfy the similarity ratio of 2:3 with the perimeter of ΔPQR (54 cm).

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their perimeters, altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors.

Area Ratio Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)².

Criteria for Similarity

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy any of the following criteria: Angle-Angle (AA), Side-Angle-Side (SAS), or Side-Side-Side (SSS).</p

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, CA is produced to P, ∠ BAP = 126°. If ∠ABC ∶ ∠ACB = 5 ∶ 2, the degree measures of ∠B and ∠C are respectively:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **Exterior Angle Theorem**, the exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite **interior angles**.

Sum of interior opposite angles ∠B + ∠C = Exterior ∠BAP = 126°.

Ratio of **∠B : ∠C** = 5 : 2.

Total units = 5 + 2 = 7 units ⇒ 126°.

1 unit = 126° ÷ 7 = 18°.

∠B = 5 × 18° = 90° and ∠C = 2 × 18° = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 90° and 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Exterior **∠BAP** = 126° and **∠ABC : ∠ACB** = 5 : 2.

**Formula Used:** Exterior angle = Sum of interior opposite angles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18027a6cf73f04149659ade221687d26c9508f79ac71dca1a39f40eb9ab66b2c.png] 

Let **∠ABC** = 5x and **∠ACB** = 2x.

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem** in triangle ABC:

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠ACB = Exterior ∠BAP

⇒ 5x + 2x = 126°

⇒ 7x = 126°

⇒ x = 126° ÷ 7

⇒ x = 18°

Now, calculate the measure of each angle:

⇒ **∠B** = 5x = 5 × 18° = 90°

⇒ **∠C** = 2x = 2 × 18° = 36°

**∴ The correct answer is 90° and 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote (opposite) interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°. In this case, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 54° + 90° + 36° = 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Here, interior ∠BAC + exterior ∠BAP = 180° ⇒ 54° + 126° = 180°.</p

questions.question: The lengths of the two sides forming the right angle of a right-angled triangle are 21 cm and 20 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the triangle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The lengths of the two sides forming the right angle of a right-angled triangle are 21 cm and 20 cm

**Formula:**

Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Circum-radius of the right-angled triangle = Hypotenuse/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0e0d3b347f3189e2a318dc58f3746b212ef4ab6366d0c537070bcfe69441c00.png] 

**Calculation:**

Base = 21 cm and Perpendicular = 20 cm

⇒ (Hypotenuse)² = 21² + 20²

⇒ 441 + 400

⇒ 841

⇒ (Hypotenuse) = √841 = 29

∴ Circum-radius of the right-angled triangle = 29/2 = 14.5 cm

questions.question: ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent respectively. If AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°, then m ∠D + m ∠C = __ __ .
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent respectively. 

AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°

Concept used:

1. SAS Congruency: If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and included angle of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent. E.g.: if ∠A = ∠X and AB/XY = AC/XZ then ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ.

From the congruency, 

AB/XY = BC/YZ = AC/XZ

and ∠B = ∠Y and ∠C = ∠Z

2. The three interior angles of a triangle will always have a sum of 180°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b260f67f751e5db4e9f5c34668912ac09fda2ab241783a7ac7d7ef81e61aff55.png] 

​According to the concept,

Since ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent and AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°, m ∠B = m ∠E = 30°.

Also, m ∠C = m ∠F ....(1)

Hence, m ∠A = m ∠D ....(2)

​According to the concept,

m ∠C + m ∠A = (180 - 30)° ....(3)

m ∠E + m ∠F = (180 - 30)° ....(4)

From 1, 2, 3 and 4,

m ∠D + m ∠C = (180 - 30)° 

⇒ m ∠D + m ∠C = 150° 

**∴ The value of m ∠D + m ∠C is 150°.**

questions.question: The measure of one of the exterior angles of a triangle is twice one of the interior opposite angles and the measure of the other interior opposite angles is 60º. The triangle is a/an:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The measure of one of the exterior angles = 2 × one of the interior opposite angles

The measure of other interior opposite angles = 60° 

**Concept used:**

Equilateral triangle: the measure of each interior angle is 60° 

Right-angle triangle: the measure of one of the interior angle should be 90° 

Scalene triangle: the measure of each angle is different.

Isosceles triangle: the measure of one of the two interior angles are equal.

The measure of one of the exterior angle = the sum of its opposite interior angles.

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle = 180° 

**Calculation:**

Let one of the interior opposites angles be x

The measure of one of the exterior angle = x + 60° 

⇒ 2 × one of the interior opposite angles = x + 60° 

⇒ 2x = x + 60° 

⇒ 2x - x = 60° 

⇒ x = 60° 

Now the third interior angle = 180° - x - 60° 

⇒ 180° - 60° - 60° 

⇒ 180° - 120° 

⇒ 60° 

Then we can see that each interior angle = 60° and this is possible when triangle will be an equilateral triangle.

**∴ The triangle is an Equilateral triangle.**

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** As we know,

∠TPS = (∠TQP - ∠PRQ)/2

24 = (78 - ∠PRQ)/2

78 - ∠PRQ = 24 × 2 = 48

∠PRQ = 78 - 48 = 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given: **

 In ΔPQR, PT ⊥ QR at T and PS is the bisector of ∠QPR

∠PQR = 78° and ∠TPS = 24° 

**Calculation:**

In ΔPQT,

∠QPT = 180° - ∠PQR - ∠PTQ = 180° - 78° - 90° = 12°

∠SPQ = ∠QPT + ∠TPS = 12° + 24° = 36°

Since PS is the bisector of ∠QPR.

∠QPR = 2 × ∠SPQ = 2 × 36° = 72°

In ΔPQR,

∠PRQ = 180° - ∠PQR - ∠QPR = 180° - 78° - 72° = 30°

**Hence the required answer is 30° **
